key_insight: The paper shows that one-step diffusion students do not need to share the exact same latent space as their teachers to learn effectively. It introduces cross-space distillation, enabling compact models to inherit knowledge from modern high-capacity diffusion teachers like SD 3.5 and Flux.
problem_solved: Existing timestep distillation methods assume teacher and student operate in the same latent space, which blocks transferring knowledge from modern diffusion teachers to smaller deployment-friendly students with different latent resolutions or VAE parameterizations.
method: Formalize cross-space distillation as a setting where teacher and student work in different latent spaces.
Design a training strategy that transfers teacher knowledge across mismatched representations rather than requiring shared latents.
Enable one-step student models to benefit from stronger modern teachers while remaining compact and practical for deployment.
impact: This makes it possible to distill state-of-the-art diffusion capabilities into smaller models that are easier to deploy. For practitioners, it expands the set of teachers that can be used and improves the path to efficient, high-quality one-step generation.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram of a modern teacher model and a smaller student model with different latent spaces

paper_title: Cross-Space Distillation: Teaching One-Step Students with Modern Diffusion Teachers
paper_authors: Anh Nguyen, Ngan Nguyen, Duc Vu, Trung Dao, Viet Nguyen
